questions.question_text: If a test-optional program allows applicants to submit GRE scores, what does the available data suggest about their impact on the chances of being accepted?
options: Submitting scores is discouraged by these programs.
Applicants who submit scores are generally less likely to be accepted.
Submitting scores gives applicants a competitive edge.
There is no correlation between submitting scores and acceptance rates.
questions.explanation: According to the provided data, 87% of applicants who submit their GRE scores to test-optional programs are accepted, suggesting that submitting scores can provide a competitive advantage.

questions.question_text: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the flexibility of taking the GRE?
options: It must be taken on specific, limited dates each year.
It is available to take year-round at various locations or at home.
It can only be taken once every six months.
It is only available at a few selected test centers worldwide.
questions.explanation: The text states that the GRE is available 365 days a year at over 1,000 locations and can also be taken at home.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the retake policy for the GRE?
options: Students can retake the test once every 21 days, up to five times per year.
Students are not allowed to retake the test once they have achieved a score.
Students can only retake the test once in their lifetime.
Students must wait at least one year before they are eligible to retake the test.
questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions that students can take the GRE once every 21 days, for a maximum of five times in a 12-month period.

questions.question_text: How do graduate and professional programs typically evaluate applicants?
options: They rely solely on standardized test scores.
They only consider the undergraduate GPA.
They evaluate candidates holistically using multiple factors.
They exclusively prioritize personal essays and recommendations.
questions.explanation: The text explains that graduate and professional programs evaluate candidates holistically, considering GRE scores alongside GPA, recommendations, essays, and experience.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the primary goal of the GRE General Test?
options: To test specific knowledge of graduate subjects
To measure critical skills developed over time that predict success in graduate school
To replace undergraduate GPA in all admissions decisions
To determine if a student is eligible for a scholarship
questions.explanation: The text states the GRE measures skills like verbal and quantitative reasoning and critical thinking, which are developed over time and predict graduate success.

questions.question_text: Based on the provided text, why might an applicant prefer to use the ScoreSelect® option?
options: It automatically increases their score on the test
It allows them to send only their best scores to programs
It provides a discount on the testing fee
It removes the need to take the test more than once
questions.explanation: ScoreSelect® is explicitly described as an option that lets test-takers choose which scores they submit to schools, allowing them to send their strongest results.

questions.question_text: Why is it advantageous for a prospective student to research various graduate admission tests?
options: To ensure they pick the test that best aligns with their goals and personal strengths
To avoid paying the testing fee
Because all graduate schools require every available test
To bypass the need for an application essay
questions.explanation: Researching different tests helps an applicant compare their options, such as the GRE versus GMAT or LSAT, to determine which test fits their specific academic path.

questions.question_text: According to the provided myths and realities, what is the reality for applicants applying to test-optional programs?
options: Submitting scores is discouraged by committees
Submitting scores gives applicants an edge
Submitting scores has no impact on acceptance
Test-optional programs do not accept GRE scores at all
questions.explanation: The text clarifies that even in test-optional programs, 87% of applicants who submit GRE scores are accepted, and doing so provides an advantage.

questions.question_text: What does the text suggest about the flexibility of the GRE design during the test?
options: Students must answer questions in a rigid, linear order
Students can skip questions and return to them later, and review/change answers
Students have no control over the timing of the sections
Students are required to finish every section in exactly 30 minutes
questions.explanation: The GRE design allows students to tag questions to skip them, return later, and review or change answers within a section.

questions.question_text: If a student claims that business and law schools prefer other tests like the GMAT or LSAT, how does the text correct this?
options: By stating that GMAT and LSAT are more difficult
By noting that over 1,300 business schools and 100+ law schools accept the GRE
By claiming that the GRE is the only test accepted by law schools
By stating that GMAT and LSAT scores are invalid for 5 years
questions.explanation: The text directly refutes this myth by pointing out the large number of business and law programs that accept the GRE.

questions.question_text: What is the primary reason given for why admissions committees do not rely on test scores alone?
options: Test scores are often inaccurate
Admissions committees evaluate applicants holistically
Test scores are not accepted by law schools
GRE scores are only valid for one year
questions.explanation: The text explains that scores are just one factor in a holistic evaluation that includes GPA, recommendations, and personal experience.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the validity of GRE scores?
options: They are valid for 2 years
They are valid for 3 years
They are valid for 5 years
They never expire
questions.explanation: The test information specifies that GRE scores remain valid for 5 years.

questions.question_text: Why might a student take the GRE early, according to the text?
options: To get a discount on the next attempt
Because scores are valid for 5 years, allowing for flexible planning
Because the test is only offered once a year
To avoid having to write a personal statement
questions.explanation: The 5-year validity period allows students to take the test early in their educational journey to keep their future options open.

questions.question_text: What does the data suggest about the outcome for students who retake the GRE?
options: Most students see their scores decline
70% of students improve their scores
There is no correlation between retaking and score improvement
Retaking the exam is prohibited
questions.explanation: The ETS data cited in the text indicates that 70% of students who choose to retake the test see an improvement in their scores.
